It was a small thing, but it made my day special.
That's why this jogging episode is so memorable for me.

A27.title: Tả chuyến du lịch trong nước

meta.en: Tell me about a trip you took in your country. Where did you go, and what did you do there?

A27.md:
One of my most memorable domestic trips was to Da Nang with three close friends about two years ago.
We stayed for four days and three nights, which felt like just the right amount.
We checked out the Marble Mountains, My Khe Beach, the Dragon Bridge, and Ba Na Hills.
The highlight for me was spending a full day at the beach — swimming in the morning and just relaxing under the sun in the afternoon.
The seafood was outstanding.
We found this small local restaurant near the beach with incredibly fresh grilled fish and shrimp at really affordable prices.
One funny memory was getting lost on the way there and stumbling upon a lively local night market by accident.
We ended up spending an hour browsing — one of those unplanned moments that turns out to be the best part of the trip.
I'd love to go back someday.

A28.title: Miêu tả điểm du lịch (ở đâu, làm gì, với ai)

meta.en: Describe a place you have traveled to. Where is it, what did you do there, and who did you go with?

A28.md:
I'd like to describe a trip to Hoi An — a charming ancient town in central Vietnam.
I went with two university friends and we spent three days exploring.
Hoi An is famous for its well-preserved old quarter, lantern-lit streets, and traditional crafts.
During the day we wandered through the old town, had some custom clothes made at a tailor, and rented bicycles to explore the rice paddies and nearby beaches.
At night, the town transforms into something magical — streets glowing with colorful lanterns reflected in the river.
We had dinner at a traditional restaurant overlooking the water and I still remember how peaceful it was.
What made the trip special wasn't just the scenery but the pace.
Hoi An felt like stepping back in time, and it reminded me how valuable it is to slow down sometimes.

A29.title: Miêu tả một quốc gia bạn đã đi nghỉ ở nước ngoài

meta.en: Tell me about a country you have visited on vacation. What was it like?

A29.md:
I had the chance to visit South Korea for a short work trip, and I made the most of my days off to do some sightseeing.
I visited Seoul, and I was immediately struck by how clean, organized, and efficient the city is.
The metro system was incredibly convenient — easy to navigate even without knowing much Korean.
I visited Gyeongbokgung Palace, which was stunning — traditional Korean architecture surrounded by modern skyscrapers.
I also explored Insadong for traditional crafts and Myeongdong for street food and shopping.
The food was a real highlight — bibimbap, Korean BBQ, tteokbokki... all delicious.
What impressed me most was how ancient culture and cutting-edge technology coexist so seamlessly.
It was a short visit, but it left a strong impression.
I'd love to go back for a proper holiday.

A30.title: Lý do mọi người thích đi du lịch? Lý do nào quan trọng nhất?

meta.en: Why do you think people like to travel? Which reason do you think is the most important?

A30.md:
I think people travel for all sorts of reasons, and each one is completely valid.
Some people travel to relax and escape the stress of daily life — just getting away from familiar surroundings can be incredibly refreshing.
Others go to experience new cultures, food, and perspectives.
And many people travel for adventure — hiking, diving, exploring landscapes they've never seen.
And of course, some travel specifically to spend quality time with family or friends and create shared memories.
If I had to pick the most important reason... I'd say gaining new perspectives.
Travel forces you out of your comfort zone and shows you there are many different, equally valid ways of living.
That kind of experience makes you more empathetic, open-minded, and genuinely grateful for your own life.

A31.title: Kỷ niệm về chuyến du lịch đáng nhớ

meta.en: Tell me about a memorable trip you have taken. What happened that made it so memorable?

A31.md:
The most memorable travel experience I've had was a solo trip to Sapa in northern Vietnam.
It was my first time traveling completely alone, which felt both exciting and a little daunting, to be honest.
I took an overnight train from Hanoi and arrived in the early morning surrounded by misty mountains and rice terraces.
It was breathtaking.
I joined a local trekking group and spent two days hiking through villages of ethnic minority communities.
One moment that really stood out — a local family invited me into their home for tea.
We couldn't really communicate because of the language barrier, but the warmth and hospitality they showed me was genuinely touching.
That experience taught me that human connection doesn't always need words — kindness is universal.
It remains one of the most meaningful trips I've ever taken.

A32.title: Những thứ cần chuẩn bị khi đi du lịch

meta.en: What do you do to prepare for a trip? Tell me about everything you need to get ready.

A32.md:
I like to plan carefully, but without over-scheduling everything.
The first thing I do is research the destination — must-see places, local food, weather, transport options.
Then I book accommodation and transport in advance, especially if it's peak season.
For packing, I have a checklist: weather-appropriate clothes, toiletries, medication, a basic first-aid kit, and copies of important documents.
I always bring a portable power bank since I rely heavily on my phone for navigation, translation, and photos.
I also download offline maps and save key addresses in case I lose internet connection.
A bit of local cash is always useful, and I make sure to share my itinerary with a family member so someone knows where I am.
Good preparation really does let you relax and enjoy the trip.

A33.title: Miêu tả nơi muốn du lịch và đưa lời khuyên cho Jiwon

meta.en: Describe a place you would like to visit. Also, give some travel advice to Jiwon, who is planning to visit your country.

A33.md:
A place I've always wanted to visit is Japan — specifically Kyoto during cherry blossom season.
I'm drawn to Japan because of its perfect blend of ancient tradition and modern innovation.
Kyoto appeals to me for its temples, tea houses, bamboo groves, and peaceful gardens.
I imagine walking through the Arashiyama bamboo forest in the early morning, before the crowds arrive, would be extraordinary.
If I were advising my Korean colleague Jiwon on visiting Vietnam, I'd say: start with Hoi An.
It's beautiful, walkable, and gives you a completely different side of Vietnam from the busy cities.
Go early in the morning to explore the old town before the heat kicks in.
And don't miss Cao Lau — a local noodle dish that's only made properly in Hoi An.
Absolutely delicious.
Best time to visit is February to April, when the weather is dry and pleasant.

B012.title: Những nơi bạn thích đi du lịch trong nước và lý do?

meta.en: You indicated in the survey that you like to travel domestically. Tell me about some of the places you like to travel to and why you like going there?

B012.md:
There are a lot of beautiful places in Vietnam.
But there's one I like the most: Ha Long Bay.
It is a bay in the north of Vietnam.
I love it there because I like walking along the shore, gazing at the sea and the starry sky in the evening.
And the natural scenery there is very beautiful: there are thousands of small islands in Ha Long Bay with different shapes.
I stand on the ship, go around the islands and see their beauty clearly.
Additionally, there are many kinds of seafood, and the prices are quite affordable.
This is why I make it a point to visit Ha Long Bay every summer.

B013.title: Bạn chuẩn bị những gì trước mỗi chuyến đi?

meta.en: Can you tell me about the things you do in order to prepare for trips?

B013.md:
I'm a light packer, so when I travel, I only bring the essentials.
Firstly, I pack a couple of clothes depending on the weather.
Then I add some basic emergency medicine.
I also bring a hat, sunglasses and a swimsuit.
Of course, I need a toothbrush, toothpaste, and shampoo for the trip.
And I cannot forget to bring my wallet, my phone and a charger.
That is all I need for my trip.

B014.title: Kể một trải nghiệm du lịch khó quên: khi nào, ở đâu, với ai, chuyện gì xảy ra?

meta.en: Tell me about one travel experience you had that was unforgettable. Start by telling me when this happened, where you were, and who you were with. Tell me about all the things that happended that make this experience so unforgettable?

B014.md:
Last summer, during a company team-building trip, I had quite an unpleasant experience.
After lunch, I believe I ate something that was not fresh.
Soon after, my stomach started hurting, and I developed food poisoning.
I had a high fever and a severe headache throughout the afternoon.
I had to keep running to the bathroom due to diarrhea.
To improve my condition, I went to a pharmacy and got some medicine.
Fortunately, after taking the medicine, I started feeling better.
However, I had to stay in my room and rest the next day, missing out on all the activities during the trip.
Since then, I've learned to be much more cautious about what I eat, especially in unfamiliar situations.

B015.title: Những chuyến đi hồi nhỏ: đi đâu, với ai, làm gì?

meta.en: Tell me about some of the trips that you took in your youth. Where did you go? Who did you go with? And what did you do or see during those early trips?

B015.md:
When I was a kid, I often went to the beach with my parents each summer.
We usually stayed at a beachside hotel with a great ocean view.
During the trip, we used to swim in the ocean.
We also played with a ball and built sandcastles.
Moreover, we also looked for seashells and crabs on the beach.
In the evening, we took a walk along the beach and listened to the sound of ocean.

B016.title: Mô tả một quốc gia bạn từng đến: cảnh vật và con người ra sao?

meta.en: You indicated in the survey that you travel internationally. Could you describe for me one of the countries you've visited? What did it look like? And what were the people like there?

B016.md:
I went to Singapore last year.
It was a special trip because it was the first time I traveled by plane.
Although it is a small island country with a large population, everywhere I looked was so clean and beautiful.
People usually get around by public transport or on foot, so there are no traffic jams.
The food is delicious, but the prices are expensive.
People are friendly and hard-working.
That was such an exciting experience when I traveled overseas.

B017.title: Khi đi nước ngoài bạn thường làm những gì?

meta.en: Talk about the things that you typically do when you visit another country or overseas city.

B017.md:
When I visit another country, I try to visit the historic places there.
I try to experience the streets and go to special places in that country.
I will try to taste the local food.
Of course, I will take pictures to record the nice moments.
I also want to wear traditional clothes and take part in festivals to understand more about the life and the people there.

B018.title: Chuyến đi nước ngoài đầu tiên của bạn: khi nào, ở đâu, với ai, làm gì?

meta.en: Tell me about your first trip to another country or city. When did you go? Where did you visit? What did you do there? Who did you go with? Tell me about that trip with lots of details.

B018.md:
I went to China with some colleagues for a business trip 5 years ago.
When I arrived, I was surprised by how modern and beautiful China's capital, Beijing, was.
There were so many roads, and they were so big.
There is a huge high-speed subway system.
All around are skyscrapers.
I also had an exciting experience with the food there.
The local food is so delicious and tastes so good.
It's really a place that I want to come again.

B104.title: Bạn từng về vùng quê chưa? Cảm giác thế nào, có chuyện gì thú vị?

meta.en: Have you had any experience visiting the countryside? What did you feel when you went there? Did anything interested happen?

B104.md:
Yes, I have visited the countryside several times.
The last time was when I visited my grandparents' hometown last summer.
The air there was so fresh and clean, and the people were very friendly.
I felt really relaxed because there was no noise or traffic like in the city.
One interesting thing was that I helped my uncle catch fish in a small river.
It was my first time doing that, and it was so much fun.
That trip made me love the peaceful life in the countryside.

B105.title: Một món ăn đáng nhớ bạn thử khi đi du lịch: ở đâu, món gì?

meta.en: Please tell me about one of the memorable dishes you've tried while traveling? Where did you go and what kind of food did you try there

B105.md:
Yes, I remember one special dish I tried when I traveled to Da Nang last summer.
I tried Mi Quang, which is a famous noodle dish in that area.
It was made with yellow noodles, pork, shrimp, and a little bit of soup.
The flavor was so rich and tasty, and it was very different from the noodles in my hometown.
I really enjoyed it and even ate it again the next day before I went home.
That's why it became one of the most memorable dishes I've ever tried.

A55.title: Làm gì vào ngày nghỉ?

meta.en: What do you usually do on your days off?

A55.md:
On my days off, I try to balance rest, personal development, and seeing people.
I usually wake up a bit later than usual — around 7:30 — and start with a morning jog at the nearby park.
After that and a good breakfast, I might work on personal coding projects or catch up on tech articles.
In the afternoon, I'll often meet friends for lunch or coffee, or go explore a new part of the city.
I really enjoy discovering new cafes and restaurants — Hanoi has a fantastic food scene that I feel I've barely scratched the surface of.
In the evenings, I usually wind down with a movie or a few episodes of something.
Sometimes on weekends I'll take a short day trip to the countryside or a lake outside the city.
A good day off leaves me feeling genuinely recharged for the week ahead.

A56.title: Kỷ niệm về ngày nghỉ đặc biệt

meta.en: Tell me about a special day off that you remember. What happened?

A56.md:
One day off that stands out was last year on my birthday.
My friends organized a surprise picnic at a lakeside park outside Hanoi — without telling me anything in advance.
I thought we were just going for a casual drive.
When we arrived, there were blankets, food, a cake, and a little Bluetooth speaker already set up.
We spent the whole afternoon eating, listening to music, playing games, and watching the sunset over the lake.
It was such a simple setting, but the laughter and warmth of being surrounded by people who genuinely care... it felt extraordinary.
No fancy restaurant or expensive gift could have matched that feeling.
The best memories really do come from genuine effort and thoughtfulness, not grand gestures.

B022.title: Nghỉ ở nhà, bạn muốn gặp ai và dành thời gian với ai?

meta.en: You indicated that you take vacations at home. Who are the people you would like to see and spend time with on your vacation?

B022.md:
I am always busy with work so when I am on my vacation I just want to spend time with my family.
We do many things together.
We often go camping at the park nearby, it has a campsite with a great view.
We sometimes cook meals and watch some comedies.
Moreover, we also go to a restaurant nearby, we talk about our story while enjoying the food.
I feel very relaxed and happy with my family.
So, in the future, I still want to spend time with my family on a vacation.

B023.title: Kỳ nghỉ ở nhà gần nhất: làm gì từ ngày đầu đến ngày cuối, gặp ai?

meta.en: Describe exactly what you did during the last vacation that you spent at home? Give me a description of what you did from the first to the last day. Talk about all the people you saw and everything that you did?

B023.md:
I had a three-day vacation last month.
I spent the first day cleaning my house: I made the bed, cleaned the floor, washed the clothes and blankets, and also cleaned the kitchen and bathroom.
On the second day, I met some old friends at a coffee shop.
We talked about our jobs, our families and children, and discussed our plans for the future.
On the next day, I spent time hanging out with my family.
We went to the zoo and played many games.
After that, we went to our favourite restaurant.
We ate so much because we were very hungry at that time.
It was a very nice vacation I got last month.

B024.title: Kể một chuyện bất ngờ xảy ra trong kỳ nghỉ ở nhà.

meta.en: Could you tell me about an unusual or unexpected experience you had during a vacation you had at home? What happened? Who was involved? And why was this expericence so memorable?

B024.md:
I had an unusual experience last year, during a two-day vacation at home at the peak of a hot summer.
Unfortunately, the electricity in my house suddenly went out.
It was so awful for me without electricity in that hot weather: no fan, no air conditioner, no cooking, no television.
I called the electric company to fix the problem, but it took two days of repairs.
It took my whole vacation.
That was a really terrible vacation.

B075.title: Người nước bạn tụ họp, ăn mừng thế nào?

meta.en: Talk about gatherings or celebrations in your country? What do people do when they get together to celebrate things?

B075.md:
In my country, people often go to restaurants for gatherings or celebrations.
They enjoy food and drinks with their friends.
During the celebration, they eat, drink, cheer together, and often have wine or beer.
They talk loudly and sometimes even sing together.
They leave all their work behind and enjoy this moment.
It makes their relationship closer and more intimate.

B076.title: Lần tụ họp gần nhất của bạn: dịp gì, làm gì?

meta.en: What did you do at your last gathering or celebration? What was the occasion? Give me all the details?

B076.md:
A few weeks ago, I had a team-building event with my team members in my family's garden.
Some members went fishing, and some chased and caught chickens to prepare for lunch.
Since all of us are office workers, we were not good at cooking, so it was really hard for us to make a meal by ourselves.
However, we were good at teamwork and knew how to support each other well.
In the end, we had a delicious meal, and it turned into a meaningful day of gathering.
It was such a great occasion for our team.

B077.title: Kể một sự cố đáng nhớ trong một buổi tụ họp.

meta.en: Talk about a memorable incident that happened at a gathering or a celebration? Why was it memorable? What made it unforgettable?

B077.md:
I remember going to my friend's house for his last birthday party.
We had dinner together and had some drinks.
However, I drank too much and got drunk.
My stomach was upset and I had a light headache.
I felt like I was hanging from a tree, and I could not walk normally.
I still had a hangover the next day.
It took me quite a long time to sober up.
Since then, I've told myself to be more careful when I'm drinking.

B093.title: Người nước bạn đi đâu khi rảnh? Biển, công viên hay nơi nào khác?

meta.en: Where do people in your country go to in their free time? Do they go to beaches? Do they go to parks or any other places? What are some popular locations that people go in their free time?

B093.md:
In my country, people often gather or travel when they have free time.
When they gather, they usually go to a bar or a restaurant to eat and drink with their friends.
When they travel, they often go with family or friends to beautiful places like mountains, beaches, or parks.
Of course, some people just stay at home and take a rest in their free time.
So these are the common things people do in my country when they are free.

B094.title: Thời gian rảnh của bạn ngày xưa nhiều hay ít hơn bây giờ? Khác thế nào?

meta.en: Talk about your free time in the past. Did you have more free time or less free time back then? How was it different from your free time now?

B094.md:
I had much more free time in the past when I was a student.
At that time, I only went to school for half a day, so I had the rest of the day free.
I usually hung out with my friends or played online games.
Sometimes, I also studied by myself.
But now, after I graduated, got a job, especially when I got married with two children, I'm very busy.
I rarely have free time.
Usually, I only have a little free time at the end of the day when my kids are asleep.
At that time, I just use my phone to read some news or online articles before going to bed.
So my free time now is very different from when I was a student.

B095.title: Lần gần nhất bạn có thời gian rảnh: khi nào, làm gì, với ai?

meta.en: Tell me about the last time you had some free time When was it? What did you do? Who did you spend time with?

B095.md:
The last time I had free time was two weeks ago when I took my company's annual leave.
On the first day, I just stayed at home.
I listened to music, watched some movies, and enjoyed my meals.
On the next day, I took my child to the park, the zoo, and a children's play center.
The weather was so nice that my child enjoyed outdoor activities.
We felt very relaxed at that time.
Hopefully, I will have more free time in the future.

B096.title: Những ngày lễ phổ biến ở nước bạn: mọi người ăn mừng ở đâu, làm gì?

meta.en: Tell me about some popular holidays in your country. Where do people typically celebrate these holidays? What kinds of thing do they do to celebrate?

B096.md:
There are three big holidays in Vietnam.
They are Lunar New Year's Day, Victory Day, and National Day.
On these days, people have time off from work and they gather together.
They visit their families in their hometowns, meet friends, neighbors, and cook special meals.
They also exchange lots of presents.
These holidays are important break times in the working year for people in my country.

B097.title: Một kỷ niệm ngày lễ hồi nhỏ: ở đâu, nhớ gì?

meta.en: Tell me about a holiday memory from your childhood. Tell me where you were and what that place looked like. Tell me everything that you remember from that holiday.

B097.md:
I remember a memory from Lunar New Year's Day when I was a kid.
Like other children, I liked playing with fireworks during the holiday.
But one day, I had an accident — the firework exploded and burned my hand.
It was really painful, and I had to go to the hospital to have the wound treated and bandaged.
Since that time, I never play with fireworks anymore.
It was a really bad experience.

A40.title: Thời tiết ở thành phố của bạn – so sánh với thành phố khác và quá khứ

meta.en: What is the weather like in your city? How is it different from other cities, and from the past?

A40.md:
Hanoi has a four-season climate, which makes it quite different from Ho Chi Minh City in the south.
Ho Chi Minh City basically has two seasons — dry and rainy — and stays warm all year, around 25 to 35 degrees.
Hanoi, on the other hand, has proper winters that can drop to around 10 degrees, mild springs, hot summers, and cool autumns.
Personally, I love Hanoi's spring — the weather is mild, breezy, and really comfortable for outdoor activities.
Compared to the past, though, I feel the weather has become more extreme in recent years.
Summers seem longer and hotter, winters less predictable.
I think part of it is the urban heat island effect as the city expands, and part of it is broader climate change.
It's a concerning trend.

A41.title: Thời tiết ở nước bạn – so sánh với nước khác

meta.en: Tell me about the weather in your country. How is it different from the weather in other countries?

A41.md:
Vietnam has a tropical monsoon climate with significant regional variation.
The south has two seasons — dry from November to April, rainy from May to October.
The north, where I live, has four proper seasons.
Compared to countries like South Korea or Japan, Vietnam is significantly warmer on average.
When I visited Seoul for work, the winter temperatures were well below zero — nothing like what I experience in Hanoi.
In terms of rainfall, Vietnam gets a lot during monsoon season — heavy downpours that can cause localized flooding, especially in Hanoi.
The heat and humidity here in summer can feel pretty intense to visitors from more temperate countries.
But I do think the lush greenery and vibrant nature that comes with a tropical climate is one of Vietnam's great natural assets.

A42.title: Sự kiện đáng nhớ xảy ra do thời tiết, cách bạn giải quyết

meta.en: Tell me about a memorable event caused by the weather. How did you deal with it?

A42.md:
A weather event that stands out was a strong typhoon that hit Hanoi a few years ago.
The city issued warnings the night before, so I stocked up on food and water in advance.
The next morning the wind was incredibly strong and the rain relentless.
I decided to work from home.
But around midday, the power went out and stayed out for about six hours.
Without electricity I couldn't work or charge anything.
My laptop battery lasted about three hours, which I used for the most urgent tasks.
I ended up eating cold food and spending the afternoon reading a paperback by the window — honestly not the worst afternoon.
When the power came back, I charged everything immediately and made a note to buy a proper backup power bank.
The experience really highlighted how dependent we are on electricity in modern life.

A43.title: Thời tiết thay đổi những năm gần đây? Nguyên nhân và ảnh hưởng

meta.en: Has the weather changed in recent years? What do you think are the causes and effects of these changes?

A43.md:
I've definitely noticed that weather patterns in Vietnam have become more unpredictable and extreme in recent years.
Summers in Hanoi are getting hotter — temperatures regularly exceed 40 degrees during peak months.
Even a short rainstorm can now cause significant flooding in parts of the city.
Winters, on the other hand, have become shorter and milder, disrupting the traditional seasonal rhythm.
I think the main causes are global climate change driven by greenhouse gas emissions, combined with rapid urbanization that reduces green cover and amplifies the heat island effect.
The consequences are significant — crop failures, more severe flooding in coastal regions, and real health impacts from heat stress.
On a personal level, the increasingly hot summers are just uncomfortable — they affect how much time I can spend outdoors.
I think individuals, businesses, and governments all share responsibility to reduce emissions and adapt to these changes.

B044.title: Thời tiết nơi bạn sống: từng mùa thế nào, bạn thích mùa nào?

meta.en: Tell me about the weather at where you live? What is the weather like in each season? Which season do you personally like?

B044.md:
Vietnam has four distinct seasons: spring, summer, autumn, and winter.
The weather is very nice in spring and autumn.
The temperature is cool, and it's good for outdoor activities.
On the other hand, summer is extremely hot.
Moreover, sometimes it suddenly rains heavily with dangerous thunder.
Winter is the complete opposite.
It's freezing cold and there is no rain.
Of course, I like spring and autumn the most, for the reasons I mentioned before.

B045.title: Thời tiết hôm nay nơi bạn ở thế nào? (phiên bản: giữa thu mà vẫn nóng)

meta.en: How is the weather today at where you are? Is it cold, is it warm? Talk about today's weather in detail.

B045.md:
It is the middle of autumn today, but it's still very hot.
I can feel the high temperature even in the early morning.
The sky is clear, and I don't see any clouds.
According to the weather forecast, it will rain today, but I haven't seen any signs of rain so far.
I really hope the rain will come soon to make the weather cooler.

B045b.title: Thời tiết hôm nay nơi bạn ở thế nào? (phiên bản: đầu đông)

meta.en: How is the weather today at where you are? Is it cold, is it warm? Talk about today's weather in detail.

B045b.md:
It is the beginning of winter today, and the weather is getting colder.
I can feel the cool air, especially in the early morning and at night.
The sky is a bit cloudy, and the wind is stronger than before.
According to the weather forecast, it might rain soon, but I haven't seen any rain so far.
I hope the weather stays cool and comfortable, not too cold.

B046.title: Thời tiết nước bạn thay đổi thế nào so với hồi bạn còn nhỏ?

meta.en: How has the weather in your country changed over the years? What was the weather like when you were a child? How is it different from now?

B046.md:
Vietnam still has four distinct seasons now.
But spring and summer have become longer, while winter and autumn have become shorter.
Also, summer seems much hotter and it has a lot of rain.
When it rains heavily, many places get flooded.
Sometimes people die, and many houses and fields are damaged by the summer rain.

B047.title: Kể một trải nghiệm thời tiết khắc nghiệt (bão, lũ...) và cách mọi người ứng phó.

meta.en: Severe weather conditions can do a lot of damage. Tell me about an experience you had related to severe weather conditions. Perhaps a city was flooded or maybe businesses or schools were closed due to heavy rain, what was the problem. How did people deal with the situation?

B047.md:
I remember when a strong typhoon hit Vietnam last summer.
There were strong winds and heavy rain, and floods were everywhere.
Many people lost their lives, and many houses, cars, and fields were underwater.
It was a terrible situation, and it took a long time to recover from the damage.

B059.title: Bạn tái chế những loại đồ gì?

meta.en: Recycling is a common practice in many places. Tell me about all the different kinds of items that you recycle

B059.md:
I gather recyclables at home every day.
I put cans, bottles, plastic, paper, and glass into the recycling bin.
On average, I take them out once a week, usually on my way to work.
I think recycling is a good habit because it helps us reuse resources and protect the environment.

B060.title: Hồi nhỏ việc tái chế diễn ra thế nào? Bạn mang đồ tái chế đến đâu?

meta.en: Tell me what recycling was like when you were a child. Was there a particular place to which you took out the recyclables? Describe what it was like and what you did in detail?

B060.md:
When I was a child, I wasn't aware of the benefits of recycling, so I didn't usually do it.
I only gathered paper at school sometimes because my teacher asked me to.
But now I know recycling is a good habit, and I try to do it everywhere and whenever I can.
I recycle everything possible — like cans, bottles, plastic, paper, glass, and even metals.

A36.title: Ở nước bạn chủ yếu dùng phương tiện gì?

meta.en: What kinds of transportation do people use the most in your country?

A36.md:
In Vietnam, the most widely used form of transport is definitely the motorbike.
Almost every household owns at least one — it's affordable, cheap to run, and perfect for navigating narrow streets and heavy traffic.
In Hanoi or Ho Chi Minh City, you can see thousands of motorbikes on the road at any given time.
Public buses exist and are fairly cheap, but the routes aren't always convenient, so not everyone relies on them.
Ride-hailing apps like Grab have become huge in recent years — offering both motorbike and car options.
I personally commute by motorbike most days since my office is only about 15 minutes away.
And Hanoi's metro recently opened a new line, which is a really positive development for reducing congestion.

A37.title: So sánh phương tiện giao thông ngày xưa và bây giờ

meta.en: How has transportation in your country changed compared to the past?

A37.md:
Transportation in Vietnam has changed dramatically over the past two or three decades.
When my parents were young, bicycles were the primary way of getting around — to school, to the market, to work.
Slow, but practical and eco-friendly.
Then as the economy grew rapidly in the 90s and 2000s, motorbikes became affordable for most households and quickly replaced bicycles.
Today, the streets are dominated by motorbikes, with a growing number of private cars as well.
Ride-hailing apps and GPS navigation have also made commuting much more convenient.
The downside is severe traffic congestion and air pollution in major cities.
I think the future needs to prioritize public transport, cycling infrastructure, and electric vehicles to make cities more sustainable.

A38.title: Vấn đề gặp phải với phương tiện giao thông và cách giải quyết

meta.en: Tell me about a problem you have had with transportation. How did you deal with it?

A38.md:
The most common problem I face is traffic congestion during rush hours.
My commute normally takes 15 minutes, but during peak hours — around 7:30 to 8:30 AM — it can stretch to 40 minutes or more.
That's both time-consuming and stressful, especially with an early morning meeting.
My solution is to leave home earlier, around 7 AM, to avoid the worst of it.
Another issue is unexpected rain while riding without a raincoat.
I now always keep a compact foldable raincoat in my bag during the rainy season.
I once had a flat tyre on the way to work too, which was stressful because I wasn't near a repair shop.
Luckily a nearby resident pointed me to one just two streets away.
That experience taught me to have repair shop locations saved on my phone — just in case.

A39.title: Ký ức không tốt liên quan tới phương tiện giao thông

meta.en: Tell me about an unpleasant memory related to transportation. What happened?

A39.md:
One unpleasant memory happened about a year ago in the summer.
I was riding home from work when I got caught in a sudden, very heavy rainstorm.
I hadn't checked the forecast, and I had no raincoat with me.
The rain was so intense the road flooded in several places and visibility was really poor.
I had to pull over under a small overhang and wait for about 45 minutes, completely soaked.
What made it worse was that my phone battery died, so I couldn't call anyone or check a map.
By the time I got home, my clothes and shoes were completely waterlogged, and I ended up catching a cold the next day.
Genuinely miserable experience.
But I learned from it — now I always check the weather before heading out and carry a raincoat during the wet season.

B083.title: Người nước bạn đi lại bằng gì? Phương tiện phổ biến là gì?

meta.en: Tell me about how people get around in your country, Do they drive their own cars or take trains. What are some typical means of transportation to get around?

B083.md:
There are various types of transportation in my country.
Some people take public buses or trains to get around the city, while others use their private cars.
When traveling to a faraway place, people can take a train or an airplane, but those are not very popular in Vietnam.
The most popular vehicle is the motorbike.
Most Vietnamese people use it as their private vehicle to go to work or travel around.
Currently, it is the most suitable option considering the road conditions, traffic, and lifestyle in Vietnam.

B084.title: Bạn đi lại bằng phương tiện gì? Tự lái hay đi phương tiện công cộng?

meta.en: What means of transportation do you use to get around? Do you drive or take public transportation?

B084.md:
I have one car and one motorbike, but I usually ride my bike to work or get around.
My workplace is not far from my home, so I use my bike to save gasoline and also to protect the environment.
When I go to my hometown or need to travel somewhere far, I drive my car instead, because it is much safer for long-distance trips.
So most of the time, I ride my bike to get around.

B085.title: Hồi nhỏ bạn đi lại thế nào? Giao thông khi đó khác gì bây giờ?

meta.en: How did you travel when you were a child? Were the type of transportation different back then? Describe for me how people used to get around in your city or town?

B085.md:
When I was a kid, transportation was not as good as it is now.
There were only a few cars and buses, and they were usually very old and ran very slowly.
It was inconvenient for people when they wanted to travel far.
But now, there are so many vehicles.
I can see a lot of cars, buses, and motorbikes moving on the road.
The road and traffic infrastructure have also become much better than in the past.
It is very convenient and easy to get from place to place.
Even though there are sometimes traffic jams, they don't have too much impact on people nowadays.

A44.title: Miêu tả máy tính của bạn

meta.en: Tell me about the computer you use. What does it look like, and what do you use it for?

A44.md:
I use a Samsung Galaxy Book laptop for both work and personal use — which feels pretty fitting given where I work.
It's a 15-inch Full HD display, bright and clear, which really matters when you're staring at code for hours.
It's also relatively lightweight with a slim profile, so I can carry it to meetings or cafes without any hassle.
It has a fast processor and enough RAM to run multiple development environments simultaneously without slowing down.
Battery life is decent — I can usually get through a full workday without needing to plug in.
Working in software development, having a reliable and powerful machine is essential, and this one meets my needs well.

A45.title: Miêu tả máy tính (màn hình, âm thanh)

meta.en: Describe your computer in detail: the screen, the sound, and the things you like about it.

A45.md:
The screen is a 15-inch Full HD display with good color accuracy and brightness — comfortable to work on for extended periods.
At my office desk, I've connected an external 24-inch monitor as well, for better ergonomics and more screen space.
That dual-screen setup makes development significantly more efficient — code on one screen, browser or documentation on the other.
As for audio, the built-in speakers are decent for video calls and casual music.
But for anything more serious — watching a film or actually enjoying music — I always use my wireless earphones.
Good audio quality matters to me because music is such a regular part of my routine.

A46.title: Miêu tả điện thoại di động

meta.en: Tell me about your mobile phone. What does it look like, and what do you use it for?

A46.md:
I'm currently using a Samsung Galaxy S series smartphone — I've had it for about two years now.
The screen is a large, vibrant AMOLED display that makes everything look great, whether I'm reading or watching videos.
The camera is one of its strongest features.
I use it regularly when traveling or just out on walks, and the results are consistently impressive.
The phone handles multitasking really well, which matters since I switch between a lot of apps throughout the day.
Battery life is solid — comfortably lasts a full day with moderate to heavy use.
I use it for pretty much everything: work email, messaging, navigation, music, and mobile banking.
Working at Samsung, I'm also genuinely interested in how these features evolve with each new generation.

A47.title: Tại sao bạn muốn mua một chiếc điện thoại mới?

meta.en: Why would you like to buy a new phone? What features are you looking for?

A47.md:
My current phone has served me well for two years, but I've been thinking about upgrading for a few reasons.
First, the battery has started to degrade noticeably.
By the end of a busy day it often needs charging, whereas before it would easily last until bedtime.
Second, I'd love a better camera.
The newer Samsung models have significantly improved sensors and computational photography features.
Third, storage is getting tight — two years of photos, apps, and files have accumulated and I'm constantly managing space.
And as a software engineer, using the latest device helps me stay current with the platform's capabilities.
I'm not in a rush, but within the next few months I'll probably make the switch to the latest Samsung flagship.

A48.title: Đồ vật người Việt Nam dùng nhiều nhất

meta.en: What is the object that people in your country use the most in their daily lives? Why?

A48.md:
Without question, the object Vietnamese people use most in their daily lives is the mobile phone.
Vietnam has one of the highest smartphone penetration rates in Southeast Asia, and it's easy to see why.
People use their phones for virtually everything — calls, messaging, banking, shopping, navigation, entertainment, and food delivery.
Apps like Zalo for messaging, Grab for transport and delivery, and various banking apps have become essential daily tools.
Mobile payment is growing rapidly too — many people now pay for groceries, coffee, even street food using QR codes.
For younger generations especially, the smartphone is the central device for both work and social life.
It's genuinely hard to imagine daily life in Vietnam without one now.

A49.title: Điện thoại di động quá khứ và hiện tại

meta.en: Compare the phone you used in the past with the phone you use now. How are they different?

A49.md:
My relationship with phones has changed dramatically over the years.
My first phone, when I was about 15, was a basic Nokia feature phone.
It could make calls, send texts, and play Snake — that was pretty much it.
The screen was tiny and black and white, but I was genuinely thrilled to have it.
When I started university, I got my first touchscreen smartphone.
The difference was incredible — suddenly I had internet, apps, maps, and a camera in my pocket.
I still remember the first time I used Google Maps to navigate somewhere unfamiliar.
It felt almost magical.
My current Samsung Galaxy is a world away from that old Nokia.
The processing power alone would have seemed like science fiction to my teenage self.
The evolution in just one generation is genuinely remarkable.

A50.title: Kinh nghiệm đáng nhớ khi dùng điện thoại

meta.en: Tell me about a memorable experience you had with your phone.

A50.md:
One really memorable experience happened about a year and a half ago.
I was jogging near my apartment when I slipped on a wet surface and dropped my phone into a shallow puddle.
The screen went black almost immediately.
I panicked.
I dried it off, tried turning it on — nothing.
I searched online and found the classic advice about putting it in uncooked rice to absorb the moisture.
I left it overnight, and by the next morning it turned back on.
I was genuinely relieved — and a little amazed, honestly.
The screen glitched for a few days but eventually returned to normal.
After that I immediately bought a waterproof case and a screen protector.
It taught me how fragile and valuable these devices really are.

A51.title: Vấn đề với điện thoại (hỏng/sự cố), cách bạn giải quyết

meta.en: Tell me about a problem you had with your phone. What was it, and how did you solve it?

A51.md:
The most serious phone issue I've faced was when my previous smartphone suddenly stopped charging after about 18 months of use.
I tried different cables and adaptors — nothing worked.
The battery was draining and there was no way to charge it.
Since it was still under warranty, I took it to the official Samsung service center.
After running diagnostics, they found the charging port was faulty due to a manufacturing defect.
They replaced it free of charge under warranty, which took about a week.
During that week without my phone, I borrowed an old spare from my brother to stay reachable.
It was inconvenient, but it reminded me how much I rely on my smartphone for everyday tasks.
Now I make a habit of backing up data to cloud storage regularly — just in case.

A52.title: Internet quá khứ và hiện tại; kinh nghiệm dùng Facebook đáng nhớ

meta.en: How has the internet changed compared to the past? Also, tell me about a memorable experience you had on Facebook.

A52.md:
Internet usage in Vietnam has changed beyond recognition over the past 15 years.
When I was in middle school, internet meant going to a PC café and paying by the hour for slow connections.
Websites took ages to load, streaming video was basically impossible.
Now I have fast 4G and 5G on my phone and fiber optic broadband at home.
I can stream 4K video, join video calls, and upload large files with no issues at all.
As for a memorable Facebook experience — a few years ago, an old school friend I hadn't spoken to in about eight years sent me a message out of nowhere.
He'd seen some photos I'd posted and reached out.
We ended up meeting for coffee and catching up on everything.
That reconnection was one of the most pleasant surprises social media has given me.
We've stayed in touch regularly ever since.

A53.title: So sánh Internet hiện tại và quá khứ

meta.en: Compare how people use the internet now with how they used it in the past.

A53.md:
The contrast between internet use now and 10 to 15 years ago is pretty extraordinary.
In the past, access in Vietnam was slow, expensive, and mostly limited to PC cafés or schools.
People used it mainly for basic browsing, email, or chatting on Yahoo Messenger.
Accessing news took time, and streaming anything was practically impossible.
Today, high-speed internet is widely available, affordable, and accessible on any smartphone, pretty much anywhere in the country.
Video calling family in perfect quality, streaming any film instantly, working remotely without technical limitations — all normal now.
The downsides are information overload, privacy concerns, and addictive usage patterns.
But on balance, the improvements to daily life and economic opportunity have been enormously positive.

A54.title: Giới thiệu về SNS (mạng xã hội), SNS hay dùng và những mặt tiêu cực

meta.en: Tell me about social networking services. Which ones do you use? What are the negative sides of SNS?

A54.md:
Social networking services have become a really integral part of modern life in Vietnam.
The most popular platforms here are Facebook, TikTok, Instagram, and Zalo — which is a local messaging and social app.
I personally use Facebook to stay connected with friends and family, and scroll through Instagram occasionally for photography and tech content.
SNS has genuine benefits — maintaining relationships across distances, staying informed, even growing small businesses.
But the negatives are significant and shouldn't be ignored.
The most serious problem is misinformation.
False news spreads faster than corrections, and many people believe things without verifying them.
Cyberbullying is another major concern, especially for young people.
Excessive social media use has also been linked to anxiety and lower self-esteem.
Personally, I try to limit my daily usage and be selective about what I engage with.

A58.title: Chuyện gọi điện cho bạn: nói gì, khi nào, bao lâu một lần

meta.en: Tell me about the phone calls you make to your friends. What do you talk about, when do you call, and how often?

A58.md:
I catch up with close friends on the phone about once or twice a week, depending on how busy everyone is.
Usually I call to check in and chat — how work's going, anything funny or interesting that happened, or to make plans to meet up.
Sometimes it's to ask for advice on something specific — a work decision, a purchase, a personal situation.
Calls typically last 15 to 30 minutes, unless we get into a really engaging topic, in which case it can go on much longer.
I prefer voice calls over text for proper conversations — you can convey tone and emotion so much more naturally.
I also regularly video call my parents, who live in another city.
At least once a week — it really helps me feel connected even though I'm far from home.

A59.title: Tình huống không nghe được điện thoại

meta.en: Tell me about a time when you could not answer a phone call. What happened?

A59.md:
There have been a few times I missed calls and it caused some inconvenience.
The most memorable was when my phone was on silent during an important work meeting.
My mother had been trying to reach me for about two hours — she wasn't feeling well and wanted some reassurance.
When I finally finished and checked my phone, there were five missed calls.
I immediately felt terrible.
I called her back right away, and thankfully it wasn't a serious emergency — just a headache and some anxiety.
But the guilt of having been unreachable stayed with me for the rest of the day.
Since then I've made a habit of checking missed calls immediately after any meeting.
And I let my family know in advance when I'll be unavailable for a while, so they don't worry.

B038.title: Mọi người thường làm gì trên internet?

meta.en: What do people do on the internet? Do they play games, watch television or watch movies? Talk about all the things people do online?

B038.md:
People do so many things on the internet these days.
They can send emails or check messages.
They post and share photos and information on social media such as Facebook or Twitter.
They also play online games, listen to music, or watch movies and video clips.
Additionally, they can do online shopping or even online banking.
With so many options available, the internet has become an essential part of daily life.

B039.title: Bạn thường làm gì trên internet? Có mua sắm online, chia sẻ video không?

meta.en: What do you usually do on the internet? Do you like to shop online? Do you like sharing videos with other people? Tell me about everything that you do online?

B039.md:
I do many things on the internet every day.
At work, I send emails and check messages.
Sometimes, I use Google search to get information or data for my job.
When I have free time, I usually surf the internet on my cell phone.
I read online articles or check Facebook and Twitter.
I also listen to music and watch videos or movies on some apps like Netflix or YouTube.
Sometimes I do online shopping.
I usually buy toys for my children or some electronic equipment.
So, these are the things I do on the internet every day.

B040.title: Trải nghiệm dùng internet thời kỳ đầu của bạn: bạn nhớ gì nhất?

meta.en: Tell me about your early experience of surfing the internet. What do you remember particularly about that experience?

B040.md:
In my experience, the internet now is very different from before.
Back in the day, the internet connection was very slow.
It took a long time to do anything online.
When I logged into my email or opened a web page, I had to wait a lot—it was too slow.
At that time, using a computer was the only way to access the internet.
But now, the internet speed has improved so much.
When I load a web page or do something online, it responds almost immediately.
Also, there are many ways to access the internet now.
You can use a computer, or just a cell phone, and surf the internet wherever you want.
That's really great!

B041.title: Bạn thích nhất điều gì ở điện thoại của mình? Vì sao?

meta.en: What do you like most about your phone? Maybe you like the camera or maybe you like certain applications. Tell me why you like those features and why?

B041.md:
The thing I like most is that I can access the internet with my phone.
When I have internet on my phone, I can do so many things.
I can read online magazines, check Facebook, Twitter, or other social networks.
I can also play online games, listen to music, and watch videos or movies.
Plus, I can do online banking or shopping easily with my phone.
So, there are tons of things I can do, and that's what I like the most.

B042.title: Chiếc điện thoại đầu tiên của bạn khác gì chiếc hiện tại?

meta.en: Tell me about the first phone you used? How was it different from the phone you use now?

B042.md:
My first cell phone was a simple phone.
I could only use it to send messages and make phone calls.
The size of the phone was also very small.
But nowadays, phones have changed a lot.
They are called smartphones.
The size is much bigger, and they have high-quality cameras to take photos and videos.
Smartphones are like small computers with operating systems.
There are many apps, and we can also access the internet anytime.
So, cell phones have changed a lot from the past, and they have made a big difference in our modern life.

B043.title: Kể lần bạn gặp rắc rối với điện thoại: vấn đề gì, xử lý thế nào?

meta.en: Tell me about a time when you had trouble while using your phone. What was the problem and how did you deal with it?

B043.md:
Currently, I'm using a smartphone that I bought a long time ago, so the battery is not good anymore.
But I don't have enough money to buy a new phone or replace the battery.
It's very inconvenient because sometimes I cannot use my phone when it runs out of battery.
To deal with this, I always carry a power bank.
When my phone is low on battery, I charge it right away.
It's just a temporary solution, but it's necessary for me at this time.

B048.title: Bạn nhắn tin với bạn bè về những chuyện gì?

meta.en: You indicated in the survey that you exchange text messages with friends. What kinds of text messages do you send? What are they about?

B048.md:
I usually keep in touch with my friends by exchanging text messages through an app called Facebook Messenger.
I talk about all kinds of things with my friends on that app.
First, we ask how each other is doing and do some catching up.
I also share pictures, video clips, and links with them.
We often talk about our work, our families, and our children.
Sometimes, we talk about trips or plans we want to go on.
So basically, there are tons of things I talk about with my friends through Facebook Messenger.

B049.title: Bạn hay nhắn tin khi nào, ở đâu, với ai?

meta.en: Tell me when and where you send text messages most often. Plus, who do you exchange text messages with?

B049.md:
I usually chat with my friends in the evening, after I finish all my daily work.
But sometimes, I also send text messages to my colleagues or customers while I'm working at the company.
I even send and reply to messages when I'm on the bus or in the car, using my cell phone.
So, that's when and where I usually send text messages.

B050.title: Kể một tin nhắn đáng nhớ bạn từng nhận: từ ai, về gì, vì sao đáng nhớ?

meta.en: Tell me about a memorable text message you got in the past. Who was it from and what was it about? What made that text message more memorable than others?

B050.md:
I remember my last birthday.
I received a lot of birthday messages.
Many of my friends sent me congratulations and best wishes.
Some of them even sent me gift vouchers as presents and said nice things to me.
I was really surprised to get so many happy messages because I didn't expect that so many people would remember my birthday.
I was very happy, and I replied to each message one by one to thank them.

B051.title: Kể lần bạn gặp rắc rối khi gửi tin nhắn và cách xử lý.

meta.en: We sometimes have problems while sending text messages. Tell me about a time when you had trouble sending a text message. Start by giving me some background and then explain what you did to deal with the situation.

B051.md:
I think I am a careful person, but sometimes I still make mistakes when sending text messages.
I remember having trouble recently when I sent a message to the wrong chat room.
It was a personal message with sensitive content, but I accidentally sent it to a work chat room.
I immediately recalled the message and apologized for my mistake.
Since then, I always double-check carefully before sending a message.
That was a really bad experience for me.

B064.title: Những loại thực phẩm nào tốt cho sức khoẻ, và vì sao?

meta.en: Many people try to eat healthy these days. What kinds of food are healthy and why are they healthy for us?

B064.md:
Nowadays, people understand food and health better than in the past, so they try to eat healthier.
First, they eat vegetables and fruits as often as they can, because these contain a lot of vitamins and fiber.
Next, they eat fish, meat, and beans, which are rich in protein.
Also, many people choose organic food whenever possible, since it is not grown with chemicals and so it is much healthier.
So, these are the types of food that are considered healthy.

B065.title: Bạn biết đến ăn uống lành mạnh thế nào? Hồi nhỏ gia đình bạn ăn uống ra sao?

meta.en: Tell me how you found out about eating healthy. Did your family eat healthy when you were growing up? Describe to me in detail how you started to eat healthy?

B065.md:
When I was a kid, my parents really cared about food and health.
They made me eat vegetables and fruits every day, and they also made me drink milk.
But when I grew older, I started choosing my own food.
Because I'm very busy on weekdays, I often eat fast food, even though I know it's not good for my health.
I think I should take care more about food that I eat to protect my health.

B066.title: Món ăn phổ biến ở nước bạn là gì? Có gì đặc biệt?

meta.en: What is a popular dish in your country? What is special about the dish? Please describle that dish in detail?

B066.md:
The most popular dish in Vietnam is Pho.
You can find it everywhere, from the North to the South, from inland to the islands.
Moreover, some Vietnamese people bring Pho when they go abroad, so now it is also well known in many countries around the world.
Pho is a type of noodle soup, usually made with beef broth and spices, topped with rice noodles and thinly sliced beef or chicken.
Some vegetables and onions are also added.
It has a very unique taste that you cannot find in any other dish.
When I travel, I always try Pho at that place to compare and find out where the best pho is.
And actually, I often eat Pho for breakfast.

B067.title: Mô tả một người khoẻ mạnh bạn biết. Điều gì khiến họ khoẻ?

meta.en: Describe a healthy person you know? What makes that person healthy? Tell me everything about the thing that make that person healthier?

B067.md:
My wife is a very healthy person.
She always makes time to work out or exercise whenever she can.
She goes to the gym twice a week, she usually goes swimming on weekends, and walks for about 30 minutes every morning.
Plus, she always eats healthy.
She says no to fast food or junk food.
She has a strong and beautiful body.
I really admire her and I try to follow her habits to become healthier.

B068.title: Bạn từng thay đổi thói quen nào vì sức khoẻ chưa? Kể về sự thay đổi đó.

meta.en: Have you ever changed a habit or a certain lifestyle for your health? Maybe you started to work out or started to eat healthy. Tell me about that change you made?

B068.md:
In the past, I was really lazy.
I ate too much and didn't exercise.
My body became very big and I was overweight.
I often got sick and had to go to the hospital more frequently.
At that point, I decided to change myself.
I cut down on the food I ate and did hard exercise every day.
Day by day, I felt the changes in my body.
I felt better inside, I lost some weight, and I got sick less often.
I will continue doing this to stay strong and healthy.

B069.title: Kể chi tiết một việc bạn làm vì sức khoẻ và tác động của nó.

meta.en: Talk about one thing that you did for your health in detail. What kind of impact did it have on your health? Give me all the details about the effect that had on your health

B069.md:
I am a very busy person, so I don't have much time to take care of my health.
But I always spend 15 minutes every morning to do push-ups.
It's a short amount of exercise, but I think it has a big impact on my health.
After doing push-ups, I feel strong and full of energy for a long working day.
My body also gets a nice shape when I keep doing push-ups every day.
Push-ups are simple, but they have a big effect on my health.

B070.title: Nhà hàng ở nước bạn trông thế nào? Thường bán món gì?

meta.en: I would like to know about restaurants in your country. What do typical restaurants look like? What kinds of food do they commonly offer?

B070.md:
There are many kinds of restaurants in my country, such as fast food restaurants, traditional restaurants, and BBQ restaurants.
But these days, BBQ restaurants are the most popular and trending.
I can find them easily almost everywhere.
They serve many kinds of meat such as pork, beef, chicken, duck, and lamb.
There are also many types of seafood like shrimp, crab, fish, octopus, and squid.
It is so great to eat grilled meat with sauce.
Among them, seafood BBQ usually attracts the largest number of diners.

B071.title: Lần gần nhất đi ăn nhà hàng: loại gì, thực đơn, ăn gì, đi với ai?

meta.en: Tell me about a restaurant you ate out recently. What kind of restaurant was it? What was their menu and what did you eat? Who did you go with? Did you like how the food tasted?

B071.md:
I remember going to a seafood BBQ restaurant with my friend last week.
It's a well-known restaurant in my area.
The food is delicious, the price is cheap, and the service is also good.
There were many kinds of seafood, such as salmon, shrimp, crab, squid, and octopus.
We had to wait a long time because the restaurant was very crowded.
The meal was so tasty.
We enjoyed the food with some beer.
We were satisfied with the meal.
It was a great dinner.

B072.title: Nhà hàng bạn hay đến hồi nhỏ: trông thế nào, ăn gì, nhớ gì nhất?

meta.en: Now, tell me about a restaurant you used to go to as a child. What was it like? What did you eat? Who did you go with? What do you remember most about that place? Tell me about that restaurant in as much detail as possible.

B072.md:
I remember there was a fast food restaurant near my house when I was a kid.
It was a small restaurant, but it always had a lot of diners.
I used to go there on weekends with my parents.
They served many types of dishes, such as pizza, hamburgers, and Korean noodles.
I usually ordered my favorite seafood pizza and a bottle of Coca-Cola.
The pizza tasted amazing.
But now, that restaurant has moved to another place, and I don't know where it is.
I really miss it and the delicious food of that restaurant.

B073.title: Người bận rộn thường ăn uống thế nào vào ngày thường?

meta.en: How do busy working people usually get their meals on weekdays? Do they order food or go to restaurants? What do they usually do?

B073.md:
People have become a lot busier than in the past.
Sometimes, they don't even have time to cook for themselves, so they eat out or order in much more often.
At the same time, people also care more about their health than before.
Even when they eat out, they think about eating healthy.
So, they tend to choose restaurants that offer healthy menus.
This has become a trend: people eat out more often, but they focus on healthier options.

B052.title: Các cửa hàng / trung tâm mua sắm ở nước bạn trông thế nào?

meta.en: You indicated in the survey that you like to go shopping. Talk about stores or shopping centers in your country. What are they like? Describe them in detail.

B052.md:
There are tons of stores in Vietnam.
They are everywhere these days, especially on crowded streets with heavy traffic.
One of the largest places to shop is outlet malls.
There are many types of stores in outlet malls.
You can buy food, clothes, furniture, electronic devices, and so on.
You can often get discounts or bargain for the price of the product you want to buy.
So, whether the store is small or large, there are plenty of stores in my country.

B053.title: Bạn đi mua sắm ở đâu, khi nào, mua gì? Nơi đó có gì đặc biệt?

meta.en: Where do you go and when do you go shopping for something? What do you buy when you go there? What is special about that place?

B053.md:
I go to various places to shop, such as outlet malls or department stores.
However, I prefer to shop online.
Nowadays, online shopping is very convenient in many ways.
It saves me time and energy when I buy the things I need.
When I want to buy food or clothes, I usually go to physical stores because I believe they should be checked directly before buying.
But for things like electronic tools, equipment, or books, I usually buy them online.
So, I go shopping whenever I need something, but overall, I prefer online shopping.

B054.title: Ký ức mua sắm hồi nhỏ: cửa hàng nào, trông thế nào, ấn tượng gì?

meta.en: Think of your early memories of shopping. Was there a store you remember from you childhood? What did it look like and what were your impressions of that place?

B054.md:
I remember there was a grocery store near my house when I was a kid.
Even though it was small, it had everything I needed.
The prices were also very cheap, and sometimes we could bargain to get a better deal.
I used to go there to buy candy, ice cream, or milk.
Sometimes I also bought toys or school supplies.
The shop owner was very friendly with customers.
That is one of my earliest memories of shopping.

B055.title: Người nước bạn thường mặc gì? Đi làm và đi chơi có khác nhau không?

meta.en: What kinds of clothes do people in your country typically wear? Do they wear different clothes for work or for play?

B055.md:
Life is very modern now.
Fashion and style are everywhere and influence everyone.
Vietnamese people are the same — they are very stylish.
They like to follow the latest fashion trends and wear different clothes for each season.
Fashion and styles also change depending on the season.
Plus, people wear different types of clothes depending on where they are — at the office, going out with friends, or attending an event.
So, I can say that people in my country are very fashionable these days.

B056.title: Bạn thích mặc kiểu gì? Hôm nay bạn mặc gì?

meta.en: What kind of clothes do you like to wear personally? What kind of fashion style do you like? What are you wearing today?

B056.md:
Today, I am wearing a black T-shirt and blue jeans.
This is also my usual style.
I like a simple and strong look.
I usually wear a T-shirt and jeans with sneakers.
Most of my clothes are white, blue, or black — very simple colors.
So, that's my style: simple and strong.

B057.title: Thời trang hồi bạn còn nhỏ khác gì bây giờ?

meta.en: Fashion styles are always changing. Tell me about the kinds of clothes that were popular when you were younger. How are they different from what is popular now?

B057.md:
Actually, when I was a kid, I didn't have enough clothes to wear.
I had to use old clothes from my brother and cousins.
Most of my friends were the same as me at that time.
So, fashion style when I was young was not very stylish.
But now, the quality of life has become much better.
There are many styles and fashion trends, and people always update themselves with the latest trends, following famous models.
I see people wearing beautiful and fashionable clothes everywhere.
So, fashion between the past and now is very different.

A60.title: Giới thiệu về ngân hàng gần nhà / ấn tượng về ngân hàng nào nhất

meta.en: Tell me about a bank near your home. Which bank impressed you the most, and why?

A60.md:
The bank I use most is Vietcombank — there's a branch about 10 minutes from my apartment.
It's a fairly modern branch with a comfortable waiting area and a well-organized queuing system.
I've visited a few times for things like account updates or processing a larger transfer that needed in- person verification.
The staff have been professional and helpful every time.
But honestly, what impresses me most is their mobile banking app.
It's fast, secure, and covers almost every transaction I need — transfers, bill payments, card management.
Since I started using it, I rarely need to visit the branch at all.
The combination of reliable in-person service and a great digital platform is what makes Vietcombank stand out for me.

A61.title: Bị vấn đề gì nên vào bệnh viện? Ký ức về việc đó / Ai giới thiệu?

meta.en: Tell me about a time you went to the hospital. What was the problem? Who recommended the hospital or the doctor?

A61.md:
About two years ago, I had to visit the hospital due to persistent stomach pain that lasted for several days.
At first I figured it was something minor — bad food, maybe — so I rested and drank plenty of water.
But when the pain got worse and started affecting my sleep, a colleague really encouraged me to get checked properly.
She recommended Dr. Hung at Viet Duc Hospital, saying he'd helped her with something similar before.
I went the next morning.
After an examination and some tests, Dr. Hung diagnosed a mild gastric inflammation, likely from stress and irregular eating habits.
He prescribed medication and dietary adjustments for three weeks.
What stood out was his patience — he explained everything clearly and answered all my questions without making me feel rushed.
The treatment worked well, and that experience taught me to take my eating habits more seriously and not delay seeking medical help.

A62.title: Bệnh viện: tại sao đi hồi bé, ký ức vui vẻ với bác sĩ tốt bụng

meta.en: Why did you go to the hospital as a child? Tell me about a happy memory with a kind doctor.

A62.md:
When I was young, I visited the hospital mainly for respiratory infections and fever — pretty standard childhood stuff.
One visit when I was about 8 stands out as a positive memory.
I had a high fever and was quite scared.
But the pediatrician who treated me was a wonderfully warm woman.
She spoke to me gently, explained every step of the examination in child-friendly language so I wouldn't be frightened.
She even gave me a small sticker at the end, which absolutely delighted me at that age.
I remember telling my mum on the way home that I wanted to be a doctor when I grew up — purely because of how kind that doctor had been.
That experience left me with a genuinely positive impression of the medical profession.
It taught me early on that the best healthcare isn't just about technical skill — the human side of medicine matters enormously.

A63.title: Lần đầu đi cắt tóc: khi nào, với ai, cảm giác như thế nào?

meta.en: Tell me about the first time you went to get a haircut. When was it, who were you with, and how did you feel?

A63.md:
My first independent haircut was when I was about 17, the summer before starting university.
Until then, my mother had always come with me to the barber and handled the communication.
This time I decided to go alone and manage it myself.
I walked into a small barbershop near our house and tried to explain what I wanted — shorter on the sides, some length on top.
Unfortunately, I was too vague and a bit nervous, so the barber made his own interpretation.
When I looked in the mirror... the result was much shorter than I'd imagined.
My eyes went wide.
I didn't say anything because I felt too awkward, paid, and left.
My friends and family teased me about it for weeks.
Looking back, it was a small but important lesson: communicate clearly and specifically — and don't be afraid to speak up.

A64.title: Kỷ niệm không tốt liên quan đến cắt tóc và cách xử lý

meta.en: Tell me about a bad experience you had at a hair salon. How did you handle it?

A64.md:
A more recent bad haircut experience happened about two years ago at a new barbershop I was trying for the first time.
I showed the barber a reference photo and explained clearly what I wanted.
He nodded confidently and said he could do it.
The end result looked nothing like the photo.
The sides were uneven and the top was way shorter than I'd asked for.
I was genuinely unhappy with it.
But this time — unlike my teenage self — I decided to say something politely.
I told him it wasn't quite what I'd hoped for and asked if he could make some adjustments to even it out.
He apologized and tried to fix it, though the damage was mostly done at that point.
I paid, left, and resolved not to go back.
The lesson: even with a clear photo, only go to a barber who comes recommended or whose work you've seen before.

A65.title: Các loại giấy tờ tùy thân ở quốc gia bạn

meta.en: What kinds of identification documents do people have in your country? How do you get one?

A65.md:
In Vietnam, the primary ID is the CCCD — the Citizen Identification Card — which replaced the old system a few years ago.
Every citizen aged 14 and above is required to have one.
It contains your name, date of birth, address, nationality, and a unique 12-digit ID number.
It's also embedded with a chip storing biometric data, making it more secure than older ID systems.
You need it in almost every official situation — opening a bank account, signing contracts, booking flights, registering a SIM card, applying for jobs.
To get one, you go to your local police station with supporting documents.
They take a photo and fingerprints, and the card is usually issued within 7 to 14 days.
If it's damaged or has incorrect information, you return to the police station and apply for a replacement.
The process is straightforward, so it's important to store the card safely and report errors immediately.

B086.title: Ngân hàng ở nước bạn trông thế nào, thường nằm ở đâu?

meta.en: Tell me about banks in your country. What do they typically look like? Where are they usually located?

B086.md:
There are a lot of banks in Vietnam.
They can be government-owned, private, or foreign banks.
Most of them are located on crowded streets with heavy traffic.
There are usually ATMs outside where I can withdraw cash.
That's what banks in my country look like.

B087.title: Bạn làm những gì từ lúc bước vào đến lúc rời ngân hàng?

meta.en: What do you do from the moment you walk into the bank until you walk out? Tell me everything about what goes on when you visit the bank?

B087.md:
When I go to the bank, I first take a number and wait for my turn.
When the bank teller calls my number, I go to the counter and take care of my business.
Most often, I check my balance and make a wire transfer.
Sometimes I exchange foreign currency, and sometimes I apply for a loan.
So these are the things I usually do when I go to the bank.

B088.title: Ngân hàng hồi bạn còn nhỏ khác gì ngân hàng bây giờ?

meta.en: Banks have definitely changed over time. Tell me about a bank you remember from your childhood. What did the bank look like? How was it different from banks today?

B088.md:
In the past, I had to go to actual banks to do my banking.
But now, I can use mobile banking anytime I want.
Banking has become a lot easier than in the past.
It takes much less time and effort.
To do mobile banking, I just need to install the app and log in with my password and security code.
I most often make wire transfers through mobile banking.
So, I think mobile banking is one of the biggest changes.

B089.title: Kể một rắc rối bạn gặp ở ngân hàng và cách giải quyết.

meta.en: Sometimes, problems can arise when you are at the bank. Tell me in detail about a problem you had that involved your bank. Maybe the bank was closed or perhaps the bank might have made some kind of problem. Tell me about how you solved that problem?

B089.md:
I remember going to the bank to get a loan urgently.
But there were so many people at the bank.
First, I pulled out a number, but there were more than ten people waiting before me.
I waited and waited, but it was still not my turn.
In the end, I had to leave and go to another bank.
Since then, I try to avoid busy hours at the bank to save time and not affect my work.

B106.title: Các loại giấy tờ tuỳ thân bạn đang có? Dùng mỗi loại khi nào?

meta.en: Can you tell me about the different identification cards you have now? When do you usually use each card?

B106.md:
I have several identification cards now.
First, I have my ID card, which I use most often for daily identification or at government offices.
Next, I have my driver's license, which I use when I drive or rent a car.
I also have my company ID card, and I use it to enter my office building every day.
Sometimes, I also use my bank card to withdraw money or make payments.
So, I use each card in different situations depending on what I need to do.

B107.title: Quy trình làm thẻ căn cước của bạn: làm gì trước, làm gì sau?

meta.en: Please tell me about the procedure you went through to get an ID card? What did you do first and what you did you do next?

B107.md:
I got my ID card when I turned 18.
First, I went to the local government office with my family.
Then, I filled out an application form and gave them my personal information.
Next, they took my photo and my fingerprints.
After that, I paid a small fee and waited for about a week.
Finally, I came back to the office to get my new ID card.
It was quite simple and didn't take much time.

B108.title: Thẻ căn cước đầu tiên của bạn: cảm giác khi nhận, thường dùng khi nào?

meta.en: Please tell me about the first ID card you got? How did you feel when you got it? When do you usually use it?

B108.md:
The first ID card I got was when I was 18 years old.
I went to the local government office to make it.
When I received my first ID card, I felt very proud and excited because it made me feel like an adult.
Since then, I usually use it when I need to verify my identity, like opening a bank account, taking an exam, or buying a train ticket.
It's a very important card that I always carry with me.

B109.title: Cảnh sát ở nước bạn thường làm gì? Trách nhiệm của họ là gì?

meta.en: What kind of things do the police officer normally do in your country? What are some of their responsibilities?

B109.md:
In my country, police officers do many important things.
They keep people safe and protect public order.
They control traffic on the streets and help when there are accidents.
They also catch criminals and investigate crimes.
Sometimes they help people who get lost or need support.
Overall, police officers work very hard to keep our community safe and peaceful.

B110.title: Mô tả một cảnh sát điển hình ở nước bạn: trang phục, xe cảnh sát.

meta.en: Please describe a typical police officer in your country? How are they dressed? what does the police car look like? Tell me about it in as much detail as possible.

B110.md:
In my country, police officers are easy to recognize.
They usually wear a green or yellow uniform with a red badge on their shoulders.
They also wear a hat of the same color, which looks very official.
Police cars in Vietnam are white with blue stripes and the word "Police" written on the side.
They often have a red and blue light on top, and you can hear their siren when they go on duty.
You can see police officers on the street, directing traffic, checking vehicles, or helping keep order.
They always look serious and professional.

B111.title: Kỷ niệm liên quan đến cảnh sát: được giúp đỡ, hoặc thấy trên phim...

meta.en: Do you have any experience or memories related to police? Maybe you had help from a police officer or you might have seen a police officer on TV or in films. Tell me what you remember about the police officer.

B111.md:
Yes, I have a memory related to the police.
A few years ago, I lost my wallet on the street when I was coming home from work.
I went to the local police station to ask for help.
The police officer there was very kind.
He asked me some questions and helped me check the CCTV camera nearby.
Luckily, someone had found my wallet and gave it to the police.
I was so happy and thankful to that officer.
Since then, I have had a good impression of police officers in my country.

A02.title: Miêu tả 2 người trong gia đình/bạn bè – điểm giống và khác nhau

meta.en: Tell me about two people in your family or among your friends. How are they similar, and how are they different?

A02.md:
Sure!
I'd love to talk about two people who are really close to me — my younger brother and my best friend Minh.
My brother is 25, works as a teacher, and honestly he's the kind of person who can light up any room — super outgoing, talkative, always in a good mood.
Minh, on the other hand, is around my age and works in finance.
He's a lot quieter and more reserved — kind of the opposite personality.
But what's interesting is that despite those differences, they actually have a lot in common.
