Both of them love being active — they jog and cycle regularly on weekends.
And they're both incredibly dependable.
Whenever I need advice or just someone to talk to, I know I can count on either of them.
I think having both types of people in my life has actually been really good for me — they balance each other out in a nice way.

A03.title: Khi nói chuyện với bạn bè thường nói về vấn đề gì?

meta.en: What do you usually talk about when you get together with your friends?

A03.md:
Hmm, when I hang out or call my friends, we usually end up talking about all sorts of things, to be honest.
Work is probably the most common topic — we swap stories about our jobs, funny office situations, or sometimes ask each other for career advice.
We also talk a lot about movies and shows.
Since I'm pretty into films, I'll often recommend something and then we'll share our thoughts afterward.
Tech comes up a fair amount too, especially since a lot of my close friends work in tech-related areas.
And sometimes — not always, but sometimes — we get into deeper stuff, like life goals, travel plans, or just... venting about a stressful week.
Honestly, I think good conversations with friends are one of the best ways to recharge and get a fresh perspective on things.

A04.title: Chủ đề khi gặp gia đình/bạn bè và ảnh hưởng của việc sống chung

meta.en: What do you talk about when you meet your family or friends? How has living together with other people influenced you?

A04.md:
When I get together with family or friends, the conversations are usually pretty lively and cover a lot of ground.
With family, we catch up on the everyday stuff — how work's going, what we've been eating, any news about relatives.
With friends it tends to be more about shared interests — movies, sports, travel plans, that kind of thing.
In terms of living together — I used to live with my family before I moved to Hanoi for work.
And that really shaped me, I think.
It taught me to be more considerate, to communicate openly, and to share responsibilities.
Now that I live alone, I do sometimes miss that energy.
But living on my own has also given me a real sense of independence and self-discipline, which I genuinely value.

A05.title: Tính cách của hai người trong gia đình/bạn bè: điểm chung và khác biệt

meta.en: Compare the personalities of two people in your family or among your friends. What do they have in common, and how are they different?

A05.md:
So, comparing my brother and Minh in terms of personality — they're actually quite different.
My brother is naturally extroverted — enthusiastic, sociable, always looking for the next thing to do or talk about.
Minh is more introverted and thoughtful.
He's the type who listens carefully before he speaks, which I really respect.
One big thing they share, though, is loyalty.
Both of them are genuinely trustworthy — neither would ever let a friend down.
They're also both really hardworking in their own fields, which I find admirable.
The biggest difference is probably how they handle pressure.
My brother stays upbeat and energetic, while Minh gets calm and analytical.
I think both approaches have their strengths.

A06.title: Điều tồi tệ xảy ra với gia đình hoặc bất đồng với gia đình

meta.en: Tell me about a difficult time or a disagreement in your family. What happened, and how was it resolved?

A06.md:
One really difficult period for my family was when my grandfather became seriously ill a few years ago.
He had to be hospitalized for several weeks, and the whole family was really worried.
My parents took turns staying at the hospital, which was exhausting — both physically and emotionally.
During that time, there were some disagreements about which hospital to go to and what treatment options to pursue.
Those kinds of tensions are pretty normal under stress, I think.
But in the end, we managed to come to an agreement through open family discussion.
Thankfully, my grandfather did recover after a few months.
And honestly, going through that together brought our family closer.
It really showed us how important communication is when things get hard.

A07.title: Chọn một mâu thuẫn với cha mẹ và kể chi tiết

meta.en: Tell me about a disagreement you had with your parents. What was it about, and how did it end?

A07.md:
The biggest disagreement I've had with my parents was about my career path after I graduated.
They really wanted me to find a stable government job close to our hometown — they were worried about job security and, I think, about the distance if I moved to Hanoi.
But I was passionate about working in tech.
I'd already received an offer from Samsung, and I knew it was the right move for me.
We had several long conversations about it — some of them got a bit heated, to be honest.
But I could tell they were coming from a place of genuine concern, not trying to control me.
I tried to explain my reasoning — that the tech industry has strong prospects, and Samsung is a well- respected company.
After a few weeks of back-and-forth, they agreed to support my decision.
And looking back, I'm really grateful for how it turned out — and for how that experience helped us communicate more openly as a family.

B028.title: Mô tả một người thân hoặc bạn bè: người đó thế nào, có gì đặc biệt?

meta.en: Describe a family or a friend you have What is he or she like? What is special about that person?

B028.md:
I'd like to share a little about my parents.
My dad and mom are similar in some ways.
They are very family-oriented, showing great love for each other and their children.
They are willing to do anything to improve and support their family.
However, they also have some differences.
My dad enjoys football, but my mom doesn't.
My mom loves cats, while my dad prefers dogs.
Sometimes, they face conflicts in family life, but they always find a way to resolve them.
That's what my parents are like.
I love them deeply, and I hope to spend more time with them in the future.

B029.title: Bạn thường làm gì khi gặp gỡ bạn bè hoặc gia đình?

meta.en: Tell me about what you commonly do with your friends or family members when you get together with them?

B029.md:
I have some friends who live near my area.
On weekends, we often meet up at a coffee shop or restaurant.
We order drinks and food, and then we start chatting.
We talk about our jobs, our families, and our plans for the future.
Sometimes, we also visit an online game store and play our favorite games together.
They are like family to me—always there to support me when I feel down.
I truly cherish them and love them so much.

B030.title: Kể lần gần đây đến thăm bạn bè / người thân: làm gì, điều gì đáng nhớ?

meta.en: Talk about a time when you visited a friend or a family member recently. What did you do when you visited them? What was memorable about that visit? Tell me everything from beginning to end.

B030.md:
Last New Year's Day, I finally returned to my hometown where my parents live.
When I visited them, I brought some gifts and also purchased some new furniture for their home.
We gathered together to celebrate the holiday.
We cooked a variety of traditional foods, especially making Chung cake, which is a traditional cake in my country for New Year's Day.
During the holiday, we enjoyed delicious meals, spent time together, visited neighbors, and attended various festivals.
We left our work behind to fully embrace and enjoy this special occasion.

B031.title: Kể lần gần đây đến thăm bạn (phiên bản: uống say ở nhà bạn).

meta.en: Talk about a time when you visited a friend or a family member recently. What did you do when you visited them? What was memorable about that visit? Tell me everything from beginning to end.

B031.md:
I remember visiting my friend's house last New Year's Day.
We had dinner together and had some drinks.
However, I drank too much and got drunk.
My stomach was upset and I had a light headache.
I felt like I was hanging from a tree, and I could not walk normally.
I still had a hangover the next day.
It took me quite a long time to sober up.
Since then, I've told myself to be more careful when drinking.

B025.title: Giới thiệu công ty bạn: loại hình, thành lập khi nào, ở đâu, sản phẩm gì?

meta.en: You indicated that you work. I would like to know about your company. What kind of company is it? When was it founded? Where is it located? What products or services does it offer?

B025.md:
I work for a large electronics company.
It's a global company that does business worldwide.
I have worked here for about 10 years.
My company is one of the most famous companies in cell phones and home appliances products.
It was founded in the late 1960s.
It was small when it first started, but now it is a huge enterprise.
The headquarters is located in Korea.
There are many factories and R&D centers in several countries, such as Vietnam, China, India, These are some details about the company I work for.

B026.title: Một ngày làm việc điển hình của bạn diễn ra thế nào?

meta.en: Tell me about your daily routine at work. What kind of work do you engage in on a normal workday? What do you typically do as soon as you arrive at the office? Tell me everything about your day at work?

B026.md:
Currently, I am working in the software development department.
My work schedule is quite flexible.
I usually arrive at the office around 8 or 9 AM.
First, I turn on my computer and check all my emails.
Then, I create a task list for everything I need to accomplish that day.
Typically, my working day is quite busy, as I have numerous tasks and projects to handle.
I have regular meetings with my colleagues every morning.
Additionally, I need to respond to and send emails to customers daily.
I often leave the office around 5 or 6 PM, but sometimes I have to work late if there are any urgent or critical issues.
This is my typical working day

B027.title: Kể về một dự án bạn làm tuần trước: loại gì, phải làm gì, họp hành ra sao?

meta.en: Now, tell me about a project you did at work last week. What kind of project was it? How did it go? What did you have to do for the project? Did you have any meetings to attend for the project?

B027.md:
I had a hard work schedule last week.
It was a new project that we had to finish within one week.
I had a lot of work to do on it.
I had to research new technologies to apply to the project.
I had to create many documents, many reports, join many meetings and update status to my boss.
It seemed like I was burnt out from overworking.
Fortunately, I finished the project on time.
Great feedback from my boss and the customer, and a project bonus for my contributions, made me really happy.

B112.title: Hệ thống giáo dục nước bạn: học bao nhiêu năm, có những cấp nào?

meta.en: I'd like to know about the educational system in your country. How long do people have to go to school to complete formal education? How many classes are there in schools

B112.md:
In Vietnam, students start school at the age of six.
First, they go to primary school for five years, from grade 1 to grade 5.
Then they move to secondary school for four years, from grade 6 to grade 9.
After that, they go to high school for three years, from grade 10 to grade 12.
When they finish high school, they can take the national exam to enter university or college.
So, in total, people study around 12 years to complete formal education in Vietnam.

B113.title: Giáo dục tiếng Anh ở nước bạn: bạn học tiếng Anh thế nào?

meta.en: Tell me about English education in your country. How did you learn English as a second language? Please tell me about it in as much detail as possible.

B113.md:
In Vietnam, students start learning English from primary school.
We study grammar, vocabulary, reading and writing in class.
Later, many students go to private English centers to practice speaking and listening.
I started learning English at school, but I improved more by watching English movies and listening to songs.
Now, I try to speak English every day to get better.

B114.title: Giáo dục công lập nước bạn đã thay đổi thế nào? Cách cải thiện quan trọng nhất?

meta.en: There might have been changes in public school education in your country. What are they? What do you think is the most important way to improve public education in your country?

B114.md:
Yes, there have been many changes in public schools in Vietnam.
Now students use computers and the internet more for studying.
English and soft skills are also more important than before.
To improve public education, I think we should have more good teachers and modern facilities.
That will help students learn better and be more creative.

AR01.title: Chuyến du lịch có vấn đề – gọi điện cho đại lý đổi lịch

meta.en: I'd like to give you a situation and ask you to act it out. There is a problem with the trip you booked, so you need to change the schedule. Call the travel agency and ask to reschedule.

AR01.md:
Hi, this is Son calling.
I booked a two-day trip to Da Nang through your agency last week — it was scheduled for this Saturday the 10th.
Something unexpected has come up at work, so unfortunately I won't be able to travel on that date.
Is there any chance I could reschedule to the following Saturday, the 17th?
Could you also check whether the hotel and transport arrangements can be moved to the new date as well?
If there are any rescheduling fees, just let me know the amount and how I can take care of it.
I'd really appreciate your help.
Could you give me a call back once you've confirmed availability?
Thank you so much.

AR02.title: Giúp đỡ người nước ngoài bị lạc đường

meta.en: A foreigner on the street looks lost. Offer to help, and explain how to get to the place they are looking for.

AR02.md:
Excuse me — are you lost?
Can I help?
Oh, you're looking for Hoan Kiem Lake!
No worries at all — it's not far from here.
Just head straight down this street for about 200 meters, then turn left at the big intersection.
You'll see a red pedestrian bridge — the lake is just past that, on your right.
Should take about 10 minutes on foot.
If you have Google Maps open, I can show you exactly on your screen.
No problem at all!
Welcome to Hanoi — I hope you have a great visit!

AR03.title: Mua giày tập bị bất tiện – đến cửa hàng giải thích

meta.en: You bought a pair of running shoes, but there is a problem with them. Go to the store, explain the situation, and ask for a solution.

AR03.md:
Hello, I bought a pair of running shoes here about a week ago and I've run into a problem with them.
The sole on the left shoe has started coming apart at the front edge — and I've only worn them three or four times for light jogging.
I have the receipt and the shoes are still in the original box.
I believe this is a manufacturing defect, not damage from use — I've been wearing them completely normally.
I'd like to either exchange them for a new pair of the same model and size, or get a refund if that model's no longer available.
Could you help me with this?
I'd really appreciate a quick resolution — thank you.

AR04.title: Mất đồ trên taxi – gọi điện tới công ty taxi

meta.en: You left something in a taxi. Call the taxi company, describe the item, and ask for help getting it back.

AR04.md:
Hello, I'd like to report a lost item.
I took one of your taxis about an hour ago.
I traveled from Dinh Tien Hoang Street in Hoan Kiem District to Galaxy Building in Cau Giay District.
When I got home, I realized I'd left my laptop bag on the back seat.
It's a black bag with a grey strap, and it contains my work laptop and some important documents.
I have the receipt with me — it was taxi number 58K-12345 at around 5:40 PM.
Could you please check with the driver?
I'll come to collect it immediately if it's been found.
Please contact me at this number — thank you so much, I really appreciate your help.

AR05.title: Ở khách sạn lâu ngày – hỏi lễ tân về chỗ vui chơi gần đó

meta.en: You are staying at a hotel for several days. Ask the receptionist three or four questions about things to do nearby.

AR05.md:
Good afternoon!
I've been staying here for three days now and I have a free afternoon today.
Could you recommend some interesting things to do or places to visit nearby?
I'm especially interested in local food — are there any well-known street food areas or traditional restaurants within walking distance?
I'd also love to see some cultural or historical sites if there are any close by.
And is there anywhere I could rent a bicycle?
I'd love to cycle around and explore.
If possible, could you write down the names of the places for me?
My Vietnamese reading isn't very strong, so having it written out would be really helpful.
Thank you so much!

AR06.title: Hỏi Ava (máy tính) về nơi ở của nó

meta.en: Ask Ava three or four questions about where she lives.

AR06.md:
Hey Ava!
I have a fun question for you today — where do you actually live, or where are you located?
Do you have a physical home somewhere, or do you exist entirely in digital space?
As a software engineer, I find it genuinely interesting to think about where AI systems actually run.
Are you hosted on dedicated servers, or distributed across cloud infrastructure in multiple data centers around the world?
And does the concept of 'home' mean anything to you, or is location completely irrelevant from your perspective?
I'm really curious to hear your answer — or your best attempt at one!

AR07.title: Gọi điện cho bạn hỏi cách sử dụng máy MP3

meta.en: You borrowed an MP3 player from a friend. Call your friend and ask three or four questions about how to use it.

AR07.md:
Hey Minh, it's Son!
Sorry to bother you — do you have a few minutes?
So I just borrowed an MP3 player and I'm having trouble figuring it out.
How do I skip between songs?
Every time I press the button it just goes to a menu instead of the next track.
And how do I adjust the volume?
I pressed what looked like the volume buttons but the track changed instead.
Oh, and is there a way to create a playlist, or does it just play everything in order?
I know it sounds basic but I genuinely haven't used one of these in years!
Thanks so much — I really appreciate it.

AR08.title: Mượn máy MP3 nhưng làm hỏng – giải thích và đưa ra phương án giải quyết

meta.en: I'm sorry, but there is a problem you need to resolve. You broke the MP3 player you borrowed from your friend. Call your friend, explain the situation, and suggest two or three solutions.

AR08.md:
Hey Minh, I need to talk to you about something — and I want to apologize in advance.
I accidentally dropped your MP3 player earlier today while I was jogging, and the screen cracked.
I feel really terrible about it — I should have been more careful with something I borrowed.
I completely take responsibility, and I want to make it right.
I'd like to pay for the screen repair, or if that's not practical, I'll replace it with a new equivalent model — whichever works better for you.
Could you check how much a repair would cost?
Or if you'd prefer a replacement, just let me know what you'd want.
Again, I'm really sorry — please don't hesitate to tell me how you'd like to handle it.

AR09.title: Điện thoại mới mua bị lỗi – yêu cầu 2 giải pháp từ đại lý

meta.en: You bought a new phone, but it is not working properly. Go back to the store, explain the problem, and suggest two possible solutions.

AR09.md:
Hello, I purchased a new smartphone from your store three days ago, and I've already run into a significant problem.
When I make calls, the person on the other end can barely hear me.
The microphone doesn't seem to be functioning properly.
I haven't dropped the phone or exposed it to water — the issue appeared from the very first day of use.
I have the receipt and original packaging here with me.
I'd like to request two possible solutions.
First, could you replace this unit with a brand-new one of the same model?
Alternatively, if that's not possible, could the phone be sent for warranty repair, with a temporary device provided in the meantime?
This is my primary work phone, so I'd really appreciate a quick resolution.
Thank you for your help.

AR10.title: Mua nhầm áo – gọi điện giải quyết; nhờ chủ cửa hàng tư vấn

meta.en: You bought a shirt, but it is the wrong size. Call the store to resolve the problem, and ask the owner for advice on what else to buy.

AR10.md:
Hello, I bought a shirt from your store yesterday but when I got home I realized I'd accidentally picked up a large instead of a medium.
The shirt still has all its tags on and hasn't been worn.
Would it be possible to exchange it for the correct size?
Also, while I have you on the line — I was hoping you could give me some advice.
I'm looking for a versatile casual shirt — smart enough for the office but comfortable for weekends too.
Do you have any new arrivals that might fit that description, preferably in neutral colors?
I'll bring the original shirt and receipt when I come in.
Would this afternoon work?
Thanks so much for your help!

AR11.title: Cửa sổ hỏng – gọi người sửa; gọi lại khi mãi không thấy tới

meta.en: A window in your apartment is broken. Call the building manager to report it. Then call again, because the repairman has not arrived.

AR11.md:
(Call 1 – Báo sự cố)
Hello, I'm calling to report a problem in my apartment — I'm in unit 812, Building A.
One of my bedroom windows is broken — the latch is completely stuck and I can't close it properly.
Could you arrange for a technician to come and fix it?
Rain is expected this afternoon and leaving it open could cause water damage.
Would it be possible to have someone come this morning?
(Call 2 – Follow-up)
Hello again, this is Son from unit 812.
I called this morning about the broken window and was told a technician would arrive by 2 PM.
It's now 3:30 and no one has come yet.
Could you check on the status of my request?
It's become quite urgent — it's already started raining and water is coming in through the gap.
Could you either send someone in the next 30 minutes, or at least let me know when to expect them?
I'll be available for the rest of the afternoon.
Thank you.

AR12.title: Đi làm giấy tờ tùy thân mới gặp vấn đề / giấy tờ bị sai thông tin

meta.en: You received your new ID card, but some information on it is wrong. Go to the office, explain the problem, and ask for it to be fixed quickly.

AR12.md:
(Báo lỗi)
Good morning.
I came here last month to apply for a new CCCD and I've recently received the card.
However, I noticed that my date of birth is printed incorrectly.
It shows the 15th, but the correct date is the 5th.
I have my old ID card and household registration book here to verify the correct information.
Could you please help me process a correction and reissue the card?
(Yêu cầu xử lý nhanh)
I understand this may take some time, but I have an important banking appointment next week that requires a valid ID.
Is there any way to expedite the correction, given that the error was on your end?
I'll cooperate with whatever documentation you need.
I really appreciate your help.

AR13.title: Đến tiệm bảo cắt tóc / cắt không ưng, yêu cầu cắt lại

meta.en: You are at a hair salon. Tell the barber what kind of haircut you want. After the haircut, you are not satisfied, so ask for it to be adjusted.

AR13.md:
(Yêu cầu kiểu tóc)
Hi!
I'd like a haircut please.
I'd like to keep the top at around 5 centimeters — not too short — with the sides faded on a number two.
The front should be styled slightly forward, not too pushed back.
Here's a photo on my phone that shows roughly what I'm going for.
Take your time — I'm not in a hurry at all.
(Sau khi cắt – yêu cầu điều chỉnh)
Thank you!
I really like the overall shape, but I feel the top came out a little shorter than I was hoping for.
Would it be possible to blend the sides a bit more so the transition is a bit smoother?
I know the length can't be added back, but I think a cleaner fade would really improve it.
Thanks for your patience — and I'll make sure to bring a clearer reference photo next time!

AR14.title: Công ty du lịch báo lỗi phòng – gọi điện trao đổi với bố mẹ đổi hành trình

meta.en: The travel agency called to say there is a problem with your hotel booking. Call your parents, explain the situation, and discuss how to change the itinerary.

AR14.md:
Mum, Dad — I just got off the phone with the travel agency and there's a small issue we need to sort out.
It turns out the hotel room they booked for us in Hue has had a double-booking problem, so our rooms won't be available on the original dates.
The agency has given us two options.
We can either shift the whole trip by three days to the week after, or they can arrange a different hotel of similar quality in the same city.
Personally, I think the second option is simpler — we wouldn't need to rebook our transport.
But if you'd prefer to push the dates back entirely, I can check whether we can get the time off work.
What do you think?
The agency needs an answer by tomorrow so they can finalize everything — just let me know your preference and I'll call them back right away.

AR15.title: Mua đồ bị hỏng sau khi giặt – gọi điện phàn nàn / đòi bồi thường

meta.en: A shirt you bought was damaged after one wash. Call the store to complain, and ask for a refund or a replacement.

AR15.md:
Hello, I'm calling to report a problem with a shirt I bought at your store last week.
I followed the washing instructions on the label exactly — cold water, gentle cycle, air dry.
But after washing it just once, the color has faded dramatically and the fabric seems to have weakened — there are small pulls in the threads.
I believe this is a quality defect with the garment itself, since I followed all the care instructions properly.
I still have the receipt and the shirt as evidence.
I'd like to request either a full refund or a replacement of equivalent value.
Could you let me know your returns procedure for defective items?
Thank you.

AR16.title: Kể về chuyến thăm một gia đình người bạn nước ngoài

meta.en: Have you ever visited the family of a friend from another country? Tell me about that experience in detail.

AR16.md:
I'd like to share a really memorable experience from when I visited my Korean colleague Jiwon's family home during a work trip to Seoul last year.
Jiwon very kindly invited me to have dinner at his parents' house, which I thought was a wonderful gesture.
When I arrived, his parents greeted me so warmly — even though they spoke very little English.
They'd prepared an elaborate traditional Korean dinner — galbi, japchae, all sorts of banchan side dishes, and of course kimchi.
I was a little nervous about the dining etiquette, but Jiwon guided me gently and made sure I felt comfortable the whole time.
What touched me most was the effort his family put into making a foreign guest feel genuinely welcome.
Despite the language barrier, the warmth communicated everything.
It was a humbling and heartwarming experience — a real reminder of how much we share across cultures when we approach each other with kindness.

B100.title: Diễn: Ava cũng có việc nhà phải làm — hỏi cô ấy 3–4 câu về trách nhiệm ở nhà.

meta.en: I also have my responsibilities at home. Please ask me three or four questions about my responsibilities?

B100.md:

First, what kind of house chores do you usually do?
How often do you do them?
Do you share your responsibilities with your family members?
And which house chore do you like or dislike the most?
That's all I want to ask.
Thank you.

B101.title: Diễn: Tháng sau bạn đến một thành phố mới — gọi cho bạn ở đó, hỏi 3–4 câu để lên kế hoạch.

meta.en: You are going to visit a new city next month. Call your friend in the city and ask three or four questions to help you plan a successful trip

This is Toan.

First, can you tell me some nice places to visit there?
Also, what's the best way to get around the city — by bus, subway, or taxi?

And one more thing, what's the weather like these days?
I want to pack the right clothes.
Thanks a lot!
Talk to you soon.
